about.title: About
about.subtitle: Engineer, author, speaker
about.bio:
Becoming an expert in tomorrow's systems, somewhere between AI and cybersecurity. I want nothing more than to be a Swiss army knife companies can rely on.

I like the technical side, but I like project management even more. I run some alone, like LanceOS, my own platform, and others as a team, because succeeding together is still what I find most satisfying.

LanceOS, then: a web application for French freelancers and independent workers. Its promise fits in one sentence, it does not replace Indy. Were you expecting more? Most independent workers already use Indy, Tiime or Abby. LanceOS does not try to replace them, it brings the essentials together in one place: client tracking, which is the heart of the platform, engagements, and invoicing as an option.

On the experience side, I do not stop at my own projects. Two years of apprenticeship in web development and infrastructure, then a cybersecurity analyst internship abroad, in Bucharest between April and August 2026, closed with an excellent assessment from my supervisors. Since October 2026 I have been in my fifth apprenticeship year at Groupe IBS, in Lille, working on AI cybersecurity: auditing, usage mapping, awareness, security rollout and GDPR compliance. Those grounds are where my core skills come from: monitoring and incident response, web development, application security and compliance, and automation.

In short: I like understanding how things work and taking complicated problems apart. I have touched a fair range of subjects, from cybersecurity to websites, through migrations, automation, systems integration and application development.

And there is more than the technical side. Public speaking matters a great deal to me: learning, passing on, defending an idea, carrying a project that stands up. At 18 I published MORSE, a book on discipline and working on oneself. One day I would like to step onto a TEDx stage as a speaker.

Outside all that: running, with a 10 km Foulée Valenciennoise finished in 49 minutes, basketball, entrepreneurship, and a lot of reading, usually in English.
